title: Diary Entry on Birthday: 6 Examples for Students
description: Diary entry birthday examples: 6 model entries about my birthday and a friend's party for kids and class 6 to 10, plus format, phrases and a page.
h1: Diary entry on my birthday (6 examples)
intro: A birthday diary entry gives the date and day, opens with **Dear Diary**, says how old you turned, tells the main moments of the day in the past tense (waking up, wishes, gifts, cake, friends), shares how you felt, and ends with a closing and your name. Below are 6 complete model entries, including one about a friend's birthday party, plus phrases, steps and a page to write your own.

writer.title: Dear diary,
writer.hint: Today I turned... and the best part was...

blocks.p: A birthday entry follows the usual diary layout. The trick is to pick the moments that mattered most, so it does not turn into a long list of presents.

ul: **Date, day and time**, for example: 3 March 2025, Monday, 10 p.m.
**Dear Diary,** on its own line.
**Opening line:** how old you are today and your first feeling of the day.
**Main moments** in order: morning, school or the party, the evening.
**Feelings and thanks:** who made the day special and why.
**Closing and name**, such as Good night, then your name.

blocks.tip: Pick one gift or moment to describe in detail instead of listing ten. One clear picture is more memorable than a long list.

blocks.p: About 80 words. Simple, happy and complete. Good for grades 2 to 5.

example.label: Short entry
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Today is my birthday. I am eight years old!
Mom and Dad woke me up with a song and pancakes.
In the afternoon, my friends came over for a party.
We played musical chairs and pin the tail on the donkey.
My cake was a unicorn with rainbow sprinkles.
I blew out all eight candles in one breath.
My favorite present was a box of paints from Grandma.
I am so happy and so full of cake.
Love,
Ellie

blocks.p: It says the age, has a morning, an afternoon and an evening feeling, and picks one favorite present. That is a full birthday entry in under 80 words.

sections.h2: Birthday diary entry in 120 to 150 words

blocks.p: This exam style model fits the usual 120 to 150 word limit for class 6 to 10. It includes school, family and a surprise.

example.label: Exam style
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Today I turned thirteen. I am officially a teenager!
The day began with Maa hugging me and putting a sweet in
my mouth before I even opened my eyes.
At school I wore my new blue shirt instead of the uniform
and handed out chocolates to my whole class. Everyone sang
for me in the morning assembly, and I went bright red.
I thought the evening would be quiet, but when I opened
the door at home, the lights flicked on and my friends
jumped out shouting "Surprise!" Papa had planned it for
a week without me suspecting a thing.
We cut a chocolate cake, played antakshari, and laughed
until we could hardly breathe.
I feel so loved tonight. Thirteen is off to a great start.
Good night,
Aditya

blocks.p: Why it works: the age is clear in the first line, there is a real surprise, the events go in order from morning to night, and it ends with a feeling. It also uses dialogue just once, which adds life without taking over.
These longer models show four very different birthdays. Use them for creative writing, class 8 to 10 practice, or ideas for your own entry.

blocks.h3: The birthday everyone forgot (or did they?)

example.label: Longer entry
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Today was my twelfth birthday, and for most of the day
I thought everybody had forgotten.
Mom just said "good morning" and rushed off to work.
My best friend Maya did not even mention it at lunch.
My little brother asked if I had finished his cereal.
By the time I walked home, I felt like crying.
Then I opened the front door. The living room was full
of balloons, and twelve people yelled "Happy birthday!"
Maya had been texting my mom all week to plan it.
I laughed and cried at the same time, which is a very
weird feeling.
We had tacos and a chocolate cake shaped like a guitar.
Lesson learned: the quiet days are sometimes the ones
where people are planning the biggest surprises.
Love,
Hannah

example.label: Longer entry
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
This is my first birthday away from my family. I turned
fifteen today at boarding school, and I was dreading it.
This morning my phone buzzed at six. It was Ammi, Abbu and
my sisters on a video call, all singing badly and holding
up a cake I could not eat. I laughed, but my throat hurt
after we hung up.
Classes were normal. Then at dinner the lights in the hall
went off, and my roommates Kwame and Luca came out of the
kitchen holding a cake with fifteen wobbly candles.
They had saved their pocket money for two weeks to buy it.
The whole hall sang. I did not know what to say.
I still miss home tonight. But I know now that family can
be the people who are with you, not only the people you
were born with.
Good night,
Tariq

blocks.p: A more thoughtful entry for older students, mixing the day with reflection.

example.label: Reflective entry
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Sixteen. It sounds so much older than fifteen did.
We had a braai at home this afternoon. Uncle Sizwe
manned the fire, Mama made her famous chakalaka, and my
cousins took about two hundred photos of the cake.
My best friend Lindiwe gave me a journal with a note inside:
"For all the things you are too shy to say out loud."
So here I am, using it on the first night.
This year I want to try out for the debate team, stop
worrying so much about what people think, and learn
to drive with Papa in the empty school car park.
I feel grateful tonight. Grateful for my family, for
Lindiwe, and for this new blank book to fill.
Here's to sixteen,
Naledi

blocks.p: Many students are asked to write about a friend's birthday party instead of their own. The format is the same.

example.label: Longer entry
example.title: Dear Diary,
example.text:
Today was my best friend Sam's birthday party, and it
was at a bowling alley!
I spent ages choosing a present and finally got him a
football shirt from his favorite team. When he opened
it, he put it on straight over his other shirt.
I am terrible at bowling. My first three balls went
straight into the gutter. Then Sam showed me how to aim
at the arrows on the lane, and I got a strike! Everyone
cheered so loudly that people at the next lane turned
round to look.
Afterwards we had pizza and a cake shaped like a
bowling pin. Sam's mum gave us each a party bag with
sweets and a little trophy.
It was not even my birthday, but it felt like one.
See you tomorrow,
Diego

sections.h2: Useful words and phrases for a birthday diary entry

ul: excited, overjoyed, thrilled, delighted, grateful, loved, special
surprised, speechless, emotional, shy, overwhelmed
a little sad, homesick, older, thoughtful
candles, cake, icing, frosting, sprinkles, balloons, streamers
presents, gifts, wrapping paper, greeting card, party bag
guests, surprise party, birthday song, wishes, celebration
I woke up feeling that today was going to be special.
My family surprised me with breakfast in bed.
I closed my eyes, made a wish and blew out the candles.
I was speechless when I opened the present.
The house was filled with laughter and music.
It was the best birthday I have ever had.
I went to bed feeling loved and very full of cake.

blocks.p: Pick a few phrases and mix them with your own real details. For other topics to practice, see our list of [diary entry topics](/diary-entry-topics/).

sections.h2: How to write your own birthday diary entry

steps.name: Write the date, day and time
steps.text: Then Dear Diary on the next line.

steps.name: Start with your age and a feeling
steps.text: "Today I turned eleven, and I woke up before the sun."

steps.name: Tell the day in order
steps.text: Morning wishes, school or the party, the evening. Two or three moments are enough.

steps.name: Describe one special moment in detail
steps.text: A surprise, a gift, a funny accident, a kind word. Add what you saw, heard or tasted.

steps.name: Say how you feel tonight and who you are thankful for
steps.text: This turns a list of events into a real diary entry.

steps.name: Close with a closing and your name
steps.text: Good night, Love, or See you tomorrow, then sign it.

sections.h2: Common mistakes in birthday diary entries

ul: **Only listing presents.** Describe one or two, then talk about people and feelings.
**Forgetting your age.** It is the first thing a reader wants to know.
**Writing it as an invitation or a speech.** A diary entry is private and looks back on the day.
**Present tense for everything.** Events go in the past tense: we cut the cake, I opened my gift.
**Missing the date, closing or name.** These are easy marks.
**No ending thought.** Finish with how you feel or a wish for the year ahead.

blocks.p: For more model answers, see our [diary entry examples](/diary-entry-examples/) and our [diary entry about the best day of my life](/diary-entry-best-day-of-my-life/). Younger writers will find more ideas in [diary for kids](/diary-for-kids/).

faq.q: How do I start a birthday diary entry?
faq.a: Write the date, day and time at the top, then Dear Diary. Your first sentence should say your new age and how you felt, for example: Today I turned twelve, and I woke up so excited that I could not stay in bed. This tells the reader what the entry is about straight away.

faq.q: What should I write in a diary entry about my birthday?
faq.a: Write how old you turned, how the day started, the main moments such as school, a party or a family meal, one special gift or surprise described in detail, who made the day special, and how you feel at the end of the day. Finish with a closing and your name.

faq.q: How many words should a birthday diary entry be?
faq.a: Follow the word limit in your question. Class 6 to 10 exam questions usually ask for 100 to 150 words. Young children can write 60 to 100 words. For creative writing homework, 200 to 300 words lets you add more detail and feelings.

faq.q: How do I write a diary entry about my friend's birthday party?
faq.a: Use the same format: date, Dear Diary, body, closing and name. Say whose party it was and where, what gift you gave, two or three fun moments, and how you felt. Remember you are still writing about your own experience, so keep it in the first person.

faq.q: Can a birthday diary entry be sad?
faq.a: Yes. Birthdays are not always happy. You might miss someone, feel forgotten, or be away from home. Writing honestly about that is what a diary is for. Try to end with one small good thing or a hope for the year ahead, which also makes a stronger ending in an exam.
